title: Finite Quadratic Weil Index
body_html:
Finite Quadratic Weil Index

This node defines the finite Gauss-sum Weil index. It is the scalar appearing in Gérardin's Fourier-Gaussian normalization. It should be distinguished from the three-Lagrangian transition cocycle \(\gamma(L,L',L'')\): that cocycle can often be computed by a Gauss-sum Weil index, but it is not the definition of the Weil index of a quadratic form.

The finite-group algebra in this node is Lean-checked in lean/FiniteQuadraticWeilIndex.lean using the Lean 4.30/mathlib project /Users/hoxide/mycodes/lean-shared. The Lean file formalizes finite quadratic characters, the unnormalized Gauss sum, the normalized Weil index after choosing a square root of \(|A|\), additive-character orthogonality, and the identity

$$ G(q)G(q^{-1})=|A|. $$

It does not formalize Gérardin's finite-field discriminant formula.

Finite Quadratic Module

Let \(A\) be a finite abelian group. A quadratic character on \(A\) is a function

$$ q:A\longrightarrow \mathbb C^\times $$

such that the function

$$ b_q(x,y):=q(x+y)q(x)^{-1}q(y)^{-1} $$

is a bimultiplicative character of \(A\times A\). The quadratic character is nondegenerate if

$$ A\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb C^\times), \qquad x\longmapsto b_q(x,-) $$

is an isomorphism.

Definition

For a nondegenerate finite quadratic module \((A,q)\), define its Weil index by the normalized Gauss sum

$$ \omega(A,q) := |A|^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in A}q(x). $$

Equivalently, if \(dx\) is the self-dual measure on \(A\), meaning

$$ \int_A f(x)\,dx = |A|^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in A}f(x), $$

then

$$ \omega(A,q)=\int_A q(x)\,dx. $$

The square root \(|A|^{1/2}\) is the positive real square root. For nondegenerate \(q\), the Weil index has absolute value one:

$$ |\omega(A,q)|=1. $$

Indeed, let

$$ G(q):=\sum_{x\in A}q(x). $$

Then

$$ \begin{aligned} |G(q)|^2 &= \sum_{x,y\in A}q(x)q(y)^{-1}\\ &= \sum_{z,y\in A}q(y+z)q(y)^{-1}\\ &= \sum_{z,y\in A}q(z)b_q(y,z). \end{aligned} $$

For fixed \(z\), the inner sum

$$ \sum_{y\in A}b_q(y,z) $$

is \(|A|\) if \(z=0\) and is \(0\) otherwise. The nonzero case is the usual orthogonality of nontrivial characters of \(A\), and nondegeneracy says that \(b_q(-,z)\) is nontrivial for every \(z\neq0\). Hence

$$ |G(q)|^2=|A|, $$

and therefore \(|\omega(A,q)|=1\).

Finite-Field Quadratic Form

Let \(k\) be a finite field of odd order \(q_0\), let \(\psi:k\to \mathbb C^\times\) be a nontrivial additive character, and let \((V,Q)\) be a finite-dimensional nondegenerate quadratic \(k\)-space. Put

$$ q_Q(v):=\psi(Q(v)). $$

Then the Weil index of \((V,Q)\) with respect to \(\psi\) is

$$ \omega_\psi(V,Q) := q_0^{-\dim V/2}\sum_{v\in V}\psi(Q(v)). $$

If

$$ Q(x_1,\ldots,x_n) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{r=1}^n a_r x_r^2, \qquad a_r\in k^\times, $$

then

$$ \omega_\psi(V,Q) = W(\psi)^n\chi\!\left(\prod_{r=1}^n a_r\right), $$

where \(\chi:k^\times\to\{\pm1\}\) is the quadratic character and

$$ W(\psi) := q_0^{-1/2}\sum_{t\in k}\psi(t^2/2). $$

The factor \(\prod_r a_r\) is the discriminant of \(Q\), up to squares. Thus the formula depends only on the dimension, the one-dimensional Gauss sum \(W(\psi)\), and the discriminant class.

Gérardin's Notation

In Gérardin Section 2.4, choose a Witt decomposition

$$ E=E_+\oplus E_-. $$

Let \(b:E_-\to E_+\) be an \(i\)-symmetric isomorphism. Gérardin's quadratic form on \(E_-\) is

$$ Q_b(y):=i(by,y). $$

With his self-dual finite measure \(dy\), the Gaussian constant is

$$ w_\tau(b) = \int_{E_-}\tau(Q_b(y))\,dy. $$

In the notation of this node,

$$ w_\tau(b)=\omega_\tau(E_-,Q_b). $$

Gérardin evaluates it as

$$ w_\tau(b) = W(\tau)^{\dim E_-}d(b)^{(1-q_0)/2}, $$

where \(d(b)\) is the discriminant of \(Q_b\). Since \(a^{(q_0-1)/2}\) is the quadratic character of \(a\), the exponent \((1-q_0)/2\) is the same quadratic-character factor, up to the harmless inverse convention.

The relation in Gérardin's Fourier normalization is

$$ \varphi(b)\,w_\tau(b)=1. $$

Thus the operator attached to an element exchanging \(E_+\) and \(E_-\) is normalized by the inverse of the finite quadratic Weil index.
